```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here::here("R", "theme_seas.R"))
# Maps fill the whole picture with sea colour (no white strips at the sides)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev.args = list(bg = "#DCE2F5"))
p <- \(f) here::here("data", "processed", f)
land <- sf::st_read(p("story_land.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
spa  <- readr::read_csv(p("seabirds_spa_change.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
tot  <- readr::read_csv(p("seabirds_species_totals.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
gtot <- readr::read_csv(p("seabirds_gannet_totals.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
pc   <- \(x) sprintf("%+d%%", round(x))
t_of <- \(sp, col) tot[[col]][tot$species == sp]

base_map <- function(xlim, ylim, title = NULL) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = land, fill = "#F3EEE3", colour = "#8F8778", linewidth = 0.3) +
    coord_sf(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 14, base_family = .eb$sans) +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#DCE2F5", colour = NA),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#DCE2F5", colour = NA),
          plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 10, 14),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          plot.title = element_text(family = .eb$sans_heavy, colour = "#111111", size = 19, margin = margin(b = 8)),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(family = .eb$mono, size = 10, colour = "#111111"),
          legend.text = element_text(family = .eb$mono, size = 9.5, colour = "#111111"))
}
# Put labels on whichever side of the point has more room
side_labels <- function(d, xlim, nudge) {
  mid <- xlim[1] + 0.62 * diff(xlim)
  d |> mutate(right = lon < mid,
              lx = ifelse(right, lon + nudge, lon - nudge),
              hj = ifelse(right, 0, 1))
}
change_fill <- scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#A3241A", mid = "#F3EEE3", high = "#1F33B5",
                                    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-100, 100), breaks = c(-100, 0, 100),
                                    labels = c("\u2212100%", "No change", "+100%"),
                                    name = "Change, baseline to 2023",
                                    guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                                                            barwidth = grid::unit(16, "lines"),
                                                            barheight = grid::unit(0.7, "lines")))
scot <- list(x = c(-9.2, 1.0), y = c(54.6, 61.0))
north <- list(x = c(-9.2, 0.6), y = c(57.3, 61.0))
shet <- list(x = c(-2.6, -0.4), y = c(59.35, 60.95))
```

::::{.cr-section}

Scotland holds some of the most important seabird colonies in the North Atlantic, many of them protected as Special Protection Areas (SPAs). These are the colonies whose 2023 counts appear in this story. @cr-colonies

:::{#cr-colonies}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
cols <- spa |> distinct(spa, lon, lat)
base_map(scot$x, scot$y, "Seabird SPAs with 2023 counts") +
  geom_point(data = cols, aes(lon, lat), shape = 21, size = 3.2, fill = "#5f6b1e", colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.8)
```
:::

In the summer of 2021, highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) was first recorded in **Great Skuas** in the UK. Scotland's northern islands hold most of the UK's Great Skuas. @cr-skua-where

:::{#cr-skua-where}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
sk <- spa |> filter(species == "Great Skua")
base_map(north$x, north$y, "Great Skua SPAs, sized by pre-outbreak count") +
  geom_point(data = sk, aes(lon, lat, size = baseline), shape = 21, fill = "#a7b544",
             colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.95) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 14, name = "Territories (baseline)")
```
:::

By the 2023 breeding season, every surveyed Great Skua colony had fewer territories. Across all nine SPAs the count fell from `r format(t_of("Great Skua", "baseline"), big.mark = ",")` to `r format(t_of("Great Skua", "count_2023"), big.mark = ",")`. @cr-skua-change

:::{#cr-skua-change}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
base_map(north$x, north$y, paste0("Great Skua: ", pc(t_of("Great Skua", "pct")), " across nine SPAs")) +
  geom_point(data = sk, aes(lon, lat, size = baseline, fill = pct), shape = 21,
             colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 14, guide = "none") + change_fill
```
:::

Shetland holds the largest colonies. Zooming in, the falls range from 40% at Ronas Hill to 86% on Noss. @cr-shetland

:::{#cr-shetland}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
sk_sh <- sk |> filter(between(lon, shet$x[1], shet$x[2]), between(lat, shet$y[1], shet$y[2]))
base_map(shet$x, shet$y, "Great Skua in Shetland and Fair Isle") +
  geom_point(data = sk_sh, aes(lon, lat, size = baseline, fill = pct), shape = 21,
             colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.6) +
  geom_label(data = side_labels(sk_sh, shet$x, 0.09),
             aes(lx, lat, label = paste0(sub(",.*| - .*", "", spa), " ", pc(pct)), hjust = hj),
             size = 3.6, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("#F3EEE3", 0.92)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 14, guide = "none") + change_fill
```
:::

In 2022 the virus hit **Northern Gannets**. RSPB reported at least 11,000 Gannet deaths across Scotland that season. Scotland's Gannet colonies include Hermaness, Noss, Fair Isle, Sula Sgeir, Ailsa Craig, and the Forth Islands, home to the Bass Rock. @cr-gannet

:::{#cr-gannet}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
gn <- spa |> filter(species == "Northern Gannet")
base_map(scot$x, scot$y, paste0("Gannet: ", pc(gtot$pct_observed_baseline), " across six SPAs")) +
  geom_point(data = gn, aes(lon, lat, size = baseline, fill = pct), shape = 21,
             colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.6) +
  geom_label(data = side_labels(gn, scot$x, 0.3),
             aes(lx, lat, label = paste0(sub(",.*| and .*", "", spa), " ", pc(pct)), hjust = hj),
             size = 3.4, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("#F3EEE3", 0.92)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 16, guide = "none") + change_fill
```
:::

Gannet colonies had been growing before the outbreak, so a simple before-and-after comparison understates the loss. Against each colony's projected 2021 size, the fall is closer to `r pc(gtot$pct_trend_adjusted)`. @cr-baseline

:::{#cr-baseline}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
tibble(baseline = factor(c("Counted baseline\n(2014 to 2021)", "Projected to 2021\n(pre-outbreak trend)"),
                         levels = c("Counted baseline\n(2014 to 2021)", "Projected to 2021\n(pre-outbreak trend)")),
       pct = c(gtot$pct_observed_baseline, gtot$pct_trend_adjusted)) |>
  ggplot(aes(baseline, pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = c("#5f6b1e", "#111111"), colour = "#111111", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pc(pct)), vjust = -0.8, colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#111111") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(-35, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Gannet change to 2023, by choice of baseline", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_seas(base_size = 15, bg = "white")
```
:::

Not every species fell everywhere. **Guillemot** counts rose at some SPAs and fell at others, and across 18 SPAs the total barely changed. Colony-level swings are a reminder not to read a single colony as the whole population. @cr-guillemot

:::{#cr-guillemot}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.5
gu <- spa |> filter(species == "Common Guillemot")
base_map(scot$x, scot$y, "Guillemot: mixed fortunes across 18 SPAs") +
  geom_point(data = gu, aes(lon, lat, size = baseline, fill = pct), shape = 21,
             colour = "#111111", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") + change_fill
```
:::

So what do the counts tell us? They show a large drop in breeding numbers that coincides with the outbreak. On their own they cannot show how much HPAI caused, whether missing birds died or skipped breeding, or whether colonies have started to recover since. @cr-colonies
